title: GATE Physics Topic Test: Electronics — Set 2
titleEn: GATE Physics Topic Test: Electronics — Set 2

questions.questionTextEn: An ideal op-amp configured with a resistor $R$ at the inverting input and a capacitor $C$ in the feedback path (non-inverting input grounded) functions as a:
questions.explanationEn: With $R$ at the input and $C$ in feedback, $V_{\text{out}}(t) = -\frac{1}{RC}\int V_{\text{in}}(t)\,dt$, forming an inverting integrator.

questions.questionTextEn: For an n-channel enhancement MOSFET in the saturation region ($V_{GS} > V_T$ and $V_{DS} \ge V_{GS} - V_T$), the drain current $I_D$ (ignoring channel-length modulation) varies with $(V_{GS} - V_T)$ as:
questions.explanationEn: In saturation, the square-law model gives $I_D = \frac{1}{2}\mu_n C_{ox}\frac{W}{L}(V_{GS} - V_T)^2$.

questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following is the main cause of thermal runaway in a BJT amplifier?
optionsEn: Increasing temperature raises reverse saturation current $I_{CBO}$ and collector current $I_C$, which increases power dissipation and raises temperature further
questions.explanationEn: Positive thermal feedback ($T \uparrow \implies I_{CBO} \uparrow \implies I_C \uparrow \implies P_D \uparrow \implies T \uparrow$) causes thermal runaway if biasing is not stabilized.

questions.questionTextEn: Which BJT configuration is primarily used as a unity-gain voltage buffer (high input impedance, low output impedance, voltage gain $\approx +1$)?
questions.explanationEn: The Emitter Follower (Common-Collector) has voltage gain $\approx +1$, high input impedance, and low output impedance, making it ideal for impedance matching.

questions.questionTextEn: In a 3-section RC phase-shift oscillator using an inverting amplifier, each RC section provides a phase shift of $60^\circ$ at $f_0 = \frac{1}{2\pi\sqrt{6}RC}$. What is the minimum inverting voltage gain magnitude $|A_v|$ required?
questions.explanationEn: At $f_0 = \frac{1}{2\pi\sqrt{6}RC}$, the 3-stage RC ladder attenuates the signal by $1/29$ with $180^\circ$ phase shift, so the inverting amplifier needs $|A_v| \ge 29$.

questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following Boolean expressions are equivalent to the NOR function $(A + B)'$?
questions.explanationEn: By De Morgan's law, $(A + B)' = A' \cdot B'$, which equals 1 iff $A = 0$ and $B = 0$. $(A' + B')' = AB$ (B false) and $A' + B' = (AB)'$ (D false).

questions.questionTextEn: A BJT in the active region has $\beta = 99$ and base current $I_B = 20\,\mu\text{A}$. What is the emitter current $I_E$ (in mA)?
questions.explanationEn: $I_E = (\beta + 1)I_B = 100 \times 20\,\mu\text{A} = 2000\,\mu\text{A} = 2.0\text{ mA}$.

questions.questionTextEn: A 4-stage binary ripple counter is clocked by a $32\text{ kHz}$ square wave. What is the output frequency at the 4th flip-flop (MSB) in kHz?
questions.explanationEn: $f_{\text{out}} = f_{\text{clk}} / 2^4 = 32 / 16 = 2\text{ kHz}$.

questions.questionTextEn: A first-order low-pass RC filter has $R = 1\,\text{k}\Omega$ and $C = 1\,\mu\text{F}$. What is its $-3\text{ dB}$ cutoff frequency $f_c = \frac{1}{2\pi RC}$ (in Hz, rounded to 1 decimal place)?
A 6-bit Flash ADC requires how many analog voltage comparators?
questions.explanationEn: An $n$-bit Flash ADC requires $2^n - 1 = 2^6 - 1 = 63$ comparators.

questions.questionTextEn: In a 555 timer configured as an astable multivibrator with $R_A = 10\,\text{k}\Omega$, $R_B = 10\,\text{k}\Omega$, and capacitor $C$, what is the duty cycle $\frac{T_{\text{high}}}{T_{\text{high}} + T_{\text{low}}}$?
questions.explanationEn: $T_{\text{high}} = 0.693(R_A + R_B)C$ and $T_{\text{low}} = 0.693 R_B C$. Duty cycle = $\frac{R_A + R_B}{R_A + 2R_B} = \frac{20}{30} = 66.7\%$.

questions.questionTextEn: An n-channel enhancement MOSFET has threshold voltage $V_T = 1\text{ V}$ and transconductance parameter $k_n = \mu_n C_{ox}(W/L) = 2\text{ mA/V}^2$. If $V_{GS} = 3\text{ V}$ and $V_{DS} = 4\text{ V}$, what is the drain current $I_D$?
questions.explanationEn: Since $V_{DS} = 4\text{ V} \ge V_{GS} - V_T = 2\text{ V}$, the MOSFET is in saturation: $I_D = \frac{1}{2}k_n(V_{GS} - V_T)^2 = \frac{1}{2}(2)(3 - 1)^2 = 4\text{ mA}$.

questions.questionTextEn: A silicon p-n junction at $300\text{ K}$ ($V_T = 25.9\text{ mV}$, $n_i = 1.5 \times 10^{10}\text{ cm}^{-3}$) has doping $N_A = 1.5 \times 10^{16}\text{ cm}^{-3}$ and $N_D = 1.5 \times 10^{16}\text{ cm}^{-3}$. What is its built-in potential $V_{\text{bi}} = V_T \ln\left(\frac{N_A N_D}{n_i^2}\right)$?
Which of the following statements about CMOS digital logic inverters (one PMOS + one NMOS) are TRUE?
optionsEn: CMOS inverters require a pull-up resistor to operate
Static power dissipation is nearly zero because in either steady logic state (0 or 1), one transistor is OFF
Dynamic power dissipation scales as $P_{\text{dyn}} = C_L V_{DD}^2 f$
The NMOS pulls the output LOW when input is HIGH, and the PMOS pulls the output HIGH when input is LOW
questions.explanationEn: A, B, and C are defining advantages of CMOS logic. CMOS uses a complementary PMOS pull-up transistor rather than a static resistor (D is false).

questions.questionTextEn: In a 2's complement 8-bit signed binary system, what is the decimal value of `11110110`?
questions.explanationEn: MSB is 1 (negative). Invert bits to `00001001` (9) and add 1 -> `00001010` (10), so the value is $-10$.

questions.questionTextEn: A silicon diode has reverse saturation current $I_0 = 1\text{ nA}$ at $27^\circ\text{C}$. Using the rule of thumb that $I_0$ doubles for every $10^\circ\text{C}$ rise in temperature, what is $I_0$ (in nA) at $67^\circ\text{C}$?
questions.explanationEn: Temperature rise is $67 - 27 = 40^\circ\text{C}$ (four $10^\circ\text{C}$ steps), so $I_0 = 1 \times 2^4 = 16\text{ nA}$.

questions.questionTextEn: How many 2-input NAND gates are minimally needed to implement a 2-input OR gate?
questions.explanationEn: By De Morgan's law, $A + B = (A' \cdot B')'$. Two NAND gates invert $A$ and $B$, and a third NAND combines them: 3 NAND gates.

questions.questionTextEn: A low-pass filter has a voltage transfer magnitude that drops at $-20\text{ dB/decade}$ above its cutoff frequency $f_c = 1\text{ kHz}$. What is the attenuation in dB at $f = 100\text{ kHz}$?
questions.explanationEn: From $1\text{ kHz}$ to $100\text{ kHz}$ is 2 decades ($10^2$), giving $2 \times 20 = 40\text{ dB}$ attenuation.

questions.questionTextEn: A 4-bit ripple counter is built using flip-flops with propagation delay $20\text{ ns}$ each. What is the maximum safe clock frequency (in MHz)?
questions.explanationEn: Total ripple delay = $4 \times 20\text{ ns} = 80\text{ ns}$. $f_{\max} = 1 / (80 \times 10^{-9}) = 12.5\text{ MHz}$.

questions.questionTextEn: An ideal op-amp has a $10\,\text{k}\Omega$ resistor from $V_{\text{in}} = 4\text{ V}$ to the inverting input, and a $20\,\text{k}\Omega$ feedback resistor. If the non-inverting input is held at $V_+ = 1\text{ V}$ (instead of ground), what is the output voltage $V_{\text{out}}$ (in Volts)?
questions.explanationEn: By superposition (or KCL at $V_- = V_+ = 1\text{ V}$): $\frac{4 - 1}{10} = \frac{1 - V_{\text{out}}}{20} \implies 0.3 = \frac{1 - V_{\text{out}}}{20} \implies 1 - V_{\text{out}} = 6 \implies V_{\text{out}} = -5\text{ V}$.
